works.abstract: ABSTRACT One‐step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl‐orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket‐site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs + , Sr 2+ and UO 2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl‐orchestrated enol‐imine to keto‐enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO 2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO2 2+ uptake of 336 mg g −1 and a Cs + permeation flux of 0.26 mol m −2 h −1 , while exhibiting suppressed Sr 2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs + /Sr 2+ and Cs + /UO 2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl‐orchestrated crystallization and pocket‐site engineering as a powerful approach for multi‐component ion separations.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge‐like pore structure, a narrow pore‐size distribution, and a high β ‐phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca 2+ rejection and a Na + /Ca 2+ separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an “electrostatic–piezoelectric synergistic enhancement” separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

works.title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
Anhui University

Key Laboratory of Precision and Intelligent Chemistry, School of Chemistry and Materials Science, Institute for Carbon Neutrality, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, People’s Republic of China.
School of Chemistry & Chemical Engineering, Anhui University, Hefei, People’s Republic of China.
works.abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

works.title: APTES‐Modified Ni‐Al LDH Incorporated Positively Charged Thin Film Nanocomposite Membrane for Enhanced Water Softening
institutions: Department of Chemical Engineering Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur Kharagpur India
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The removal of hardness ions (Mg 2+ and Ca 2+ ) remains a critical challenge for nanofiltration membranes in water softening. Conventional piperazine/trimesoyl chloride‐based polyamide membranes carry a negative surface charge, relying mostly on steric hindrance for hardness ion rejection. Conversely, polyethylenimine/trimesoyl chloride (PEI/TMC)‐based polyamide membranes exhibit a positive surface charge due to the abundance of amine groups in PEI. In this study, novel positively charged thin film nanocomposite membranes are fabricated by doping 3‐aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES)‐functionalized Ni‐Al layered double hydroxide (Ni‐Al LDH) into a PEI/TMC polyamide matrix to enhance charge‐based exclusion in addition to size‐based separation. The inherently positively charged Ni‐Al LDH is synthesized via a hydrothermal route and functionalized with APTES, which introduces additional amine groups, increases its positive charge, improves its aqueous dispersibility, and enables covalent integration into the polyamide network. This synergistic addition of positively charged APTES‐modified Ni‐Al LDH into the PEI/TMC matrix yields a high pure water flux of 75 LMH, a 2.5‐fold increase over the thin‐film composite membrane while enhancing MgCl 2 rejection from 91% to 94%. Furthermore, performance testing on a real groundwater sample demonstrates the practical applicability and robust performance of these membranes in real‐world water treatment applications.

works.title: Early scaling detection in conventional RO and CCRO systems using enhanced osmotic pressure correction
institutions: University of Duisburg-Essen
IWW Water Centre
works.abstract: Permeability, determined by dividing permeate flux by the net driving pressure, serves as a crucial parameter for process evaluation, where a decrease indicates increased hydraulic resistance e.g., due to development of scaling layers. However, using permeability as a reliable operating parameter requires detailed knowledge of solution composition and hydrodynamics beyond routinely monitored online parameters. Determining the net driving pressure remains challenging, due to the difficulty in accurately quantifying the transmembrane osmotic pressure. Complex analytical requirements, natural water fluctuations, and non-ideal solution activities make accurate osmotic pressure calculations challenging and error-prone, even when detailed water compositions are known. Consequently, any corrections to osmotic pressure applied in practice, if performed at all, are based on generic, standardized approaches. Yet precise osmotic pressure correction is indispensable for effective scaling detection and monitoring of discontinuous Closed-Circuit Reverse Osmosis (CCRO). Therefore, we demonstrated two feed-water-specific osmotic pressure correction methods: an experimental approach and a mathematical method applying least-squares optimization, both refining established generic functions correlating electrical conductivity with osmotic pressure. Both approaches were evaluated on a pilot scale using commercially available spiral-wound elements treating two distinct water matrices relevant to inland desalination: one prone to CaCO 3 scaling and the other to CaSO 4 scaling. Compared to standard generic corrections, the customized approach showed superior applicability for both conventional continuous operation and CCRO, which is particularly challenging regarding permeability correction. Customized osmotic corrections proved to be the superior choice for detecting incipient CaSO 4 scaling, outperforming all evaluated metrics.

works.title: When Selectivity Is Not Enough: Product-Centered Metrics for Environmental Separations
institutions: Vanderbilt University
King Saud University
Rice University
works.abstract: Nanofiltration (NF) has traditionally been evaluated through the lens of water production, utilizing water/solute selectivity as the primary performance metric. As NF increasingly targets selective solute fractionation for resource recovery, the focus has shifted toward solute/solute selectivity. However, relying solely on selectivity can be fundamentally misleading because it frequently misaligns with practical process objectives. Furthermore, evaluating materials strictly based on instantaneous selectivity can potentially obscure the true process-level viability. This Perspective redefines performance evaluation by establishing a unified, product-centered framework applicable across three distinct separation scenarios: recovering the permeate, the retentate, or both streams as valuable products. To this end, we introduce a new framework based on the recovery-retention diagram to evaluate generic binary separations. This framework demonstrates how separation outcomes are intrinsically governed by both membrane performance and feed composition, which can be captured by the separation trajectory. Ultimately, transitioning from a purely selectivity-based evaluation framework to a product-centered one bridges the critical gap between bench-scale material discovery and scalable process engineering.

works.abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D-COF) membranes with open porosity represent a promising class of next-generation materials, particularly for selective molecular separations. In this work, we synthesized a fluorinated 3D-COF membrane (Tam-Tfta) via a liquid–liquid interfacial polymerization reaction for the efficient removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Owing to the abundance of fluorine functional groups within the COF backbone, the membrane achieved quantitative sequestration of PFOA from wastewater at environmentally relevant concentrations (1.0 μg L–1), while maintaining a high water permeance of ∼40 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the 3D-COF membrane enables favorable, orientation-assisted interactions within its pores, facilitating effective capture of amphiphilic PFOA molecules in contaminated water. This work represents one of the first demonstrations of a pure 3D COF membrane specifically engineered for removing PFAS.

works.title: Programmable Stepped Homojunction COF Membranes for High‑Efficiency Light‑Driven Ion Pumping via Photo‐Conformational Coupling
institutions: Hainan University
State Key Laboratory of Tropic Ocean Engineering Materials and Materials Evaluation, School of Materials Science and Engineering Hainan University Haikou People's Republic of China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Bioinspired light‐driven ion pumps convert solar energy into directional ionic flux, yet low photocarrier separation efficiency and high ion migration barriers within confined nanochannels severely restrict their performance. A covalent organic framework (COF) homojunction membrane is constructed via assembling exfoliated nanosheets with accurately regulated protonation levels. Such modular assembly produces staggered band alignment without changing framework compositions, which facilitates efficient charge separation and oriented carrier migration under light irradiation to form an intrinsic electric field for ion pumping. Different from common photovoltaic effects, photoexcitation induces reversible torsional relaxation of COF skeletons to directly weaken ion‐pore wall interactions and cut ion transport kinetic barriers, which is validated by molecular dynamics simulations and in situ FTIR characterization. Benefiting from this synergistic photo‐conformational coupling, optimized homojunction membranes realize improved charge separation and decreased transport resistance. The material achieves 219% higher photocurrent and 324% larger power density than uniformly protonated counterparts, and enables uphill ion transport against a tenfold concentration gradient. A programmable fabrication route is thus proposed for COF homojunction ion pumps, and photoinduced framework torsion is confirmed as a key factor to reduce ion transport barriers.

works.title: Decoupling Physical Effects in the Interfacial Polymerization of Polyamide Membranes
institutions: Technion─Israel Institute of Technology , , ,
Rice University , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Interfacial polymerization (IP) is widely used to fabricate thin films, including polyamide (PA) for reverse osmosis (RO) desalination membranes. In this process, m-phenylenediamine (MPD) diffuses across a liquid–liquid interface into the organic phase and reacts exothermically with trimesoyl chloride (TMC) to form a thin film. Because common additives simultaneously affect monomer transport and interfacial tension (IFT), isolating the physical parameters governing interfacial instability, film morphology, and membrane formation remains challenging. Here, we decouple these parameters by comparing two common additives, sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and ethyl acetate (EA), at concentrations that yield identical IFT, thereby creating comparable initial susceptibility to instability but distinct MPD transport rates. UV–vis measurements show that EA-modulated IP significantly enhances MPD transport, while particle tracking via confocal microscopy reveals stronger interfacial instabilities. Accordingly, EA-modulated IP produces more crumpled surfaces than SDS-modulated IP, consistent with an established instability-morphology phase diagram, demonstrating that polymerization rate alone can drive the system from stable to unstable regimes. These morphological changes translate into membrane performance, with EA-modified membranes exhibiting higher water permeance without compromising salt rejection. Overall, this work establishes a systematic framework for decoupling physical attributes governing IP and a strategy for rationally leveraging additives to control film morphology and membrane performance.

works.title: A Conceptual Competitive Partition–Relay Framework for Ion Transport in Affinity-Site Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
institutions: Zhejiang University
Zhejiang University , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Ion transport through affinity-site covalent organic framework (COF) membranes couples pore entry, competitive site occupation, and long-range migration. Here, we present a conceptual competitive partition–relay framework separating bulk-to-pore partitioning, occupation of finite shared affinity sites, and transport through mobile-pore diffusion and coordination-mediated relay. The reduced flux relation (eq 20) organizes these contributions through distinct thermodynamic and kinetic descriptors, while predictive use requires independent parameter constraints unavailable in current data sets. In an exploratory comparison across four held-out COF-EOx/PAN membranes, a population/accessibility-sensitive descriptor gives a median prediction error of 2.06-fold, versus 5.90-fold for geometry alone. A second COF series illustrates nonmonotonic spacing-dependent selectivity through a phenomenological mapping. Mixed-ion tests show 1.95–9.17-fold selectivity amplification alongside normalized response sums of 0.46–0.71; these deviations cannot be uniquely attributed to finite-site competition. The framework provides a conceptual basis for future structure-informed transport predictions with independently constrained parameters.

works.title: Continuously aligned biomimetic sites in MXene membranes for rapid lithium extraction
institutions: Harbin Institute of Technology
State Key Laboratory of Urban-rural Water Resource and Environment, Harbin Institute of Technology, 73 Huanghe Road, Nangang District, Harbin, China.
works.abstract: Efficient separation of lithium ions (Li + ) from magnesium ions (Mg 2+ ) remains a central challenge for direct lithium extraction from salt lake brines due to their similar physicochemical properties. Inspired by biological ion channels, biomimetic membranes have been explored to improve Li + /Mg 2+ separation. However, most biomimetic membranes focus primarily on introducing recognition sites while overlooking the structural features of biological channels, particularly the continuous arrangement of coordination sites that facilitates efficient ion transport. Here, inspired by the continuous carbonyl coordination structure of the KcsA ion channel, 4-formylbenzo-15-crown-5 ether was periodically grafted onto poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) chains and integrated with MXene nanosheets to construct two-dimensional interlayer channels with continuously aligned crown ether recognition sites. This architecture shifts Li + transport from random diffusion to successive site-to-site hopping, reducing the effective transport energy barrier. The resulting biomimetic MXene membrane achieves a Li + flux of 0.12 mol·m −2 ·h −1 with Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of 109 and performs effectively across various salt lake brines.

works.abstract: Abstract Bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes were engineered via kombucha fermentation with the incorporation of polyethylene glycol (PEG-600 and PEG-1000, 1–2%, w/v) to tailor pore formation and enhance structural stability. Subsequently, the BC membrane was functionalized with chitosan polyampholyte (CPA) to introduce zwitterionic properties for fouling mitigation. The incorporation of 2% PEG-1000 enhances BC production and mechanical properties, with elongation increasing from 20.3% to 49.7%. The zwitterionic modification leads to reduced pore size and altered surface morphology of BC membrane. The zwitterionic CPA-BC membrane exhibits effective pretreatment performance, achieving accumulated removals of 45% for soluble silica, 35% for calcium (Ca2+), and 19% for sulfate (SO42–), while maintaining a stable flux of 20 L m–2 h–1 over 17 h. CPA-BC pretreatment mitigates surface fouling of the commercial nanofiltration (NF) membrane, as evidenced by optical coherence tomography (OCT) and digital image processing, which reveal reduced surface coverage from 99.4% to 64.8%. This contributes to reducing the rapid flux decline observed with pretreatment, from 42 L m–2 h–1 at 2 h to 29 L m–2 h–1 at 17 h, compared to a rapid decline to 7 L m–2 h–1 within 2 h without pretreatment. The findings demonstrate the technical potential of waste-derived zwitterionic BC membranes to offer an effective and sustainable pretreatment strategy for controlling silica fouling and scaling, enabling improved stability and performance of desalination systems.

works.title: Steroid Hormone Transport and Adsorption Energy in Non‐functionalized Cylindrical Nanopores: Insights From Molecular Dynamics
institutions: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology
Australian National University
works.abstract: Hydrophobic and uncharged micropollutants, such as steroid hormones, pass through nanofiltration membranes due to adsorption to the membrane polymers and gradual diffusion through the active layer. The adsorption strength is difficult to quantify as the realistic pores are complex, with sections of varying diameter, roughness/tortuosity, and functional group density hampering both computational and experimental investigations. This study employs molecular dynamics to investigate hormone adsorption and how it affects transport inside structurally uniform single-walled carbon nanotube pores with controlled diameters (0.81-3.66 nm). Results show that, with 1.9 nm diameter pores, the free energy change of adsorption (ΔGads) for 17β-estradiol - a potent female sex hormone - is as high as -76 kJ/mol, consistent with the hormone's restricted movement under water flow. The adsorption strength varies with hormone type and pore diameter - however, the clogging effect rather than ΔGads dictates the hormone movement speed. Background solvent when introduced at high concentrations can have pronounced effects. Ethanol at a molar percentage exceeding 36% forms a 'buffer' layer between the pore wall and hormone, reducing ΔGads and enhancing hormone mobility. This study differentiates adsorption from other removal mechanisms, such as retention, to advance the understanding of adsorption-transport relationship in nanofiltration for selectivity.

works.title: Nanoconfined interfacial polymerization engineers thin films with interconnected angstrom pores for ion/molecule separation
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Separation Membrane Materials, College of Chemical Engineering, Zhejiang University of Technology, Hangzhou 310014, China.
Beijing Key Laboratory for Green Catalysis and Separation, Department of Chemical Engineering, Beijing University of Technology, Beijing 100124, China.
works.abstract: Precise separation of ions and molecules in valuable ion recovery, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical manufacturing requires membranes with angstrom-scale selectivity and high permeance. Conventional polyamide (PA) membranes, limited by uncontrolled interfacial polymerization (IP), exhibit compromised microporous architectures and inadequate ion/molecule separation performance. We present a nano-template confined IP strategy using imidazole/amine-functionalized porous organic polymers (POPs) as dynamic regulators. This approach orchestrates monomer diffusion and IP reaction, enabling the growth of thin PA films with uniform, interconnected angstrom-scale pores. The resultant POP-PA membrane exhibits a salt/antibiotic selectivity of ∼80, which is twofold higher than commercial counterparts, while maintaining a water permeance of ∼15 liters per square meter per hour per bar. This performance breakthrough stems from synergistic structural refinement, where thin PA film minimizes transport resistance, and deliberately constructed interconnected uniform angstrom pores realize highly efficient ion/molecule sieving. Demonstrated in scalable membrane preparation and efficient spiral-wound module for antibiotic desalination (97.6% purity), this work provides a paradigm for next-generation membranes in high-value ion/molecule separations.

works.abstract: Hydrophobic deep eutectic solvents (HDESs) have emerged as promising alternatives to the conventional pre‐hydrolysis Kraft (PHK) process for dissolving pulp (DP) production, offering opportunities to reduce reliance on pulping chemicals and facilitate lignin valorization. This study presents the first techno‐economic analysis (TEA) of HDES‐based pulping, supported by detailed process simulations to assess the potential for industrial‐scale implementation. Four process configurations were developed to improve solvent recovery and reduce energy consumption, and their minimum selling prices (MSPs) were compared with the commercial benchmark. The results show that large‐scale implementation is primarily constrained by high energy demand, with steam consumption reaching 150 metric tons (mt) per air‐dry metric tons (ADmt), mainly due to the recovery of organic solvents used for downstream processing. Consequently, process economics are strongly influenced by powerhouse operation. Integrating hybrid ultrafiltration (UF)–nanofiltration (NF) membranes reduced the modeled energy demand by more than 40% by avoiding the need for antisolvent, lowering the minimum selling price to $1160 ADmt –1. Nevertheless, uncertainty analysis indicates an approximately 20% probability of achieving an MSP below the market price of DP. Overall, this work identifies key operational and economic bottlenecks associated with HDES‐based pulping and highlights potential strategies for improving economic competitiveness.

works.title: Progress in Preparation of Hydrophilic Polymer Brush-Grafted UiO-66-NH 2 Mixed Matrix Membranes and Their Antifouling Seawater Desalination Performance
institutions: Changsha Zhongjia Senior High School
works.abstract: Nowadays, the primary dilemma facing humanity is the gradual depletion of freshwater resources. In recent years, global warming and the rapid growth of population and industrialization have intensified this contradiction, and seawater desalination is undoubtedly the optimal solution to this problem. Currently, the most mainstream seawater desalination technology worldwide is reverse osmosis. According to data from the Global Water Intelligence, seawater reverse osmosis accounts for more than 70% of global seawater desalination capacity. Membrane fouling is one of the main limitations of reverse osmosis, including organic fouling, inorganic scaling, and colloidal fouling. Fouling leads to flux decline, increased energy consumption, shortened membrane lifespan, and requires frequent use of chemical cleaning agents, further increasing costs and environmental burden. This paper reviews membrane preparation methods and compares the performance of modified MMMs and TFNs with their respective pristine membranes. From the data, MMMs and TFNs demonstrate superior performance and are fully capable of serving as primary membrane materials for seawater desalination. Research has found that polymers are undoubtedly the most suitable for seawater desalination research. The general process involves first synthesizing UiO-66-NH 2 nanoparticles, then performing polymer brush grafting modification, followed by preparation into mixed matrix membranes and thin-film nanocomposite membranes, and then conducting performance tests on the two different membranes. Polymer brush-grafted UiO-66-NH 2 shows significant advantages in antifouling and desalination. However, long-term stability and cost control remain the core challenges facing the industrialization of this technology.

institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill , , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are anthropogenic contaminants present in natural waters worldwide, including some brackish waters. Ion-capture electrodialysis (IC-ED) captures contaminants of interest while permeating nontargeted salts. We hypothesize that IC-ED is a viable strategy for simultaneous PFAS removal and brackish water desalination because the anionic charge, bulky structure, and hydrophobic properties of PFAS could interact favorably with anion exchange membranes (AEMs), facilitating PFAS removal. Accordingly, our primary objective was to determine the feasibility of simultaneous PFAS removal and desalination using IC-ED. Further, incorporating fluorous groups into materials is an emerging strategy to improve PFAS removal. Therefore, our secondary objective was to investigate the role of AEM modification via C–H fluoroalkylation on PFAS capture during IC-ED. Results showed that during IC-ED, up to 85.8% PFAS capture was observed after 24 h (73.6% after approximately 8 h), and ≥89% desalination was achieved after approximately 8 h. Further, net PFAS desorption from AEMs during IC-ED was not detectable, and AEMs were effectively regenerated (&gt;95%) using a chemical-based desorption approach. Energy consumption for IC-ED was on the same order of magnitude as reverse osmosis, but more work is needed to optimize IC-ED for energy efficiency. Comparing the performance of unmodified and modified AEMs showed that the modified AEMs enabled limited to moderate (p &lt; 0.05) improvement in PFAS capture during IC-ED, moderately lower energy consumption, and significantly faster PFAS capture (19.2–39.5% higher rate constant) under batch conditions compared with unmodified AEMs. The generally higher PFAS capture and faster PFAS sorption kinetics by the modified AEMs may be partly attributed to fluorophilic interactions. This work establishes a proof-of-concept for simultaneous PFAS capture and desalination and demonstrates that membrane physicochemical properties affect PFAS capture during IC-ED.

works.title: Energy-Efficient Reverse Osmosis and Membrane Technologies for Industrial Water Recovery and Reuse in Saudi Arabia
institutions: Independent Researcher
works.abstract: Industrial water recovery is increasingly important in Saudi Arabia, where manufacturing expansion, freshwater scarcity and changing discharge obligations converge. Reverse osmosis offers reliable dissolved-solute removal, but its application to variable industrial effluents is constrained by osmotic pressure, membrane fouling, concentrate disposal and operational energy demand. This critical narrative review examines peer-reviewed research published between 2020 and 2025 on pressure-driven membranes, staged pretreatment, hydraulic energy recovery, high-recovery configurations and hybrid resource recovery. Unlike studies centred on seawater desalination alone, the analysis distinguishes process-water reuse from conventional potable-water production and evaluates technology choices against feed chemistry and intended end use. Evidence indicates that lowering specific energy consumption requires coordinated management of feed variability, operating recovery, membrane flux, pump performance and cleaning frequency rather than a single equipment upgrade. A Saudi-oriented framework is proposed that begins with wastewater segregation and fit-for-purpose specifications, proceeds through risk-based membrane selection, and evaluates residual brine, carbon intensity and operational resilience. The synthesis identifies persistent evidence gaps in full-scale industrial datasets, lifecycle accounting and locally validated hybrid designs. These findings support staged, measurable deployment rather than universal performance claims.

institutions: Brega Petroleum Marketing Company, Tripoli, Libya

works.abstract: Inland desalination plants produce reject brine that is difficult to dispose of when there is no access to the sea. This study evaluates the combination of two-stage reverse osmosis (RO) with solar evaporation as a pathway toward zero liquid discharge (ZLD) for inland desalination, based on twelve months of field measurements in Tripoli, Libya. The evaporation rate of RO reject brine was measured in covered evaporators at depths of 1–4 cm, and single-stage and two-stage RO configurations were simulated with the DuPont WAVE software. The annual mean evaporation rate was 2.71 kg/m2/day, ranging from 0.70 kg/m2/day in December to 5.25 kg/m2/day in June. The two-stage configuration raised the total water recovery from 75.2% to 94.0%. For 6 h of daily operation, this reduced the brine volume from 1980 to 480 L/day (75.8%) and the estimated evaporation pond area from 730.6 to 177.1 m2. These results show that increasing RO recovery before solar evaporation can considerably reduce the land needed for brine disposal at inland desalination plants.

institutions: Research Center For Membrane and Film Technology Kobe University Kobe Japan
Department of Chemical Science and Engineering Kobe University Kobe Japan
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective lithium separation requires suppressing the mobility of the competing divalent ion without imposing an equivalent transport barrier on Li + , yet these two processes remain difficult to independently regulate within confined nanochannels. Here, we report an interfacial‐interlayer engineering strategy that spatially separates competitor‐ion retention from target‐ion migration in two‐dimensional (2D) vermiculite nanochannels. Polydopamine (PDA) modification reconstructs the nanosheet interface into an Mg 2+ ‐retentive region while disfavoring prolonged residence of monovalent ions near the channel walls. Subsequent sodium lignosulfonate (SLS) incorporation extends ion‐interacting functionalities into the interlayer space, where Mg 2+ experiences further retention and suppressed migration. This sequential regulation drives the transport energetics of the two ions in opposite directions, progressively lowering the Li + transport activation barrier while increasing that of Mg 2+ . The optimized Vm@PDA8/SLS1 membrane consequently achieves a Li + permeation rate of approximately 0.26 mol m −2 h −1 and a Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of approximately 81.2, while maintaining effective separation under competitive feeds, long‐term operation, and simulated brine conditions. In addition, extending the same interfacial‐interlayer regulation to other 2D‐based nanochannels similarly enhances Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity and widens the corresponding transport‐energy separation, highlighting the broader applicability of spatially differentiated retention and migration in 2D ion‐transport channels.

works.abstract: Abstract The problem of global water stress requires creating sustainable desalination technologies suitable for small-scale and renewable-powered plants. Freeze desalination is investigated here as a low-temperature alternative based on selective ice formation and salt rejection. The study develops a dynamic MATLAB/Simulink model coupling photovoltaic generation, progressive power modulation, a subcritical CO 2 /R744 refrigeration cycle, crystallization, ice washing, condenser heat recovery, and ice melting. For the reference 24-h scenario, the crystallizer inlet temperature reaches approximately 266.5 K, the maximum ice fraction is about 0.39, the brine salinity reaches approximately 57–58 g kg −1 , and the maximum freshwater mass flow rate is about 0.30 kg s −1 . The resulting cumulative specific energy consumption (SEC), freshwater recovery ratio (R), and global COP are 36.76 kWh m −3 , 19.37%, and 2.529, respectively. These characteristics define the chosen dynamic case but do not define its technological superiority and economic competitiveness. To confirm the technological suitability of the configuration, the experimental confirmation and techno-economic assessment should be performed.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Infographic titled 'Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process-Based Assessment of Seawater Desalination Plant Operational Performance,' with three color-coded sections: Research Analysis, Research Results, and Conclusions. This work presents a performance evaluation framework for seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination plants, using the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) to assess the operational performance of the Chatt El Hilal seawater desalination plant, located at Beni Saf (western Algeria). The study develops a desalination-specific criteria tree comprising 5 main factors and 18 subcriteria, structured to reflect degradation mechanisms specific to SWRO operation, together with a four-state rating rubric used to score each subcriterion. Criterion weights were derived using FAHP based on the judgment of a five-member expert panel, and operational scores were computed for five illustrative scenarios reflecting different plant conditions. The results show that the model is sensitive to changes in individual criteria and produces composite scores consistent with the severity of the conditions specified in each scenario, illustrating its potential as a decision-support tool for identifying critical subsystems and prioritizing maintenance actions. The performance scores (Sp) obtained, ranging from 3.74 to 10, are consistent with the state of the facility as qualitatively described in each scenario.

works.abstract: Abstract As the number of contaminants in wastewater grows, membranes must possess high permeability, selective removal, and functional activity. While electrospun nanofibrous membranes have a high surface area, interconnected porosity, tunable architecture, and are mechanically processable, polymers are often insufficiently selective in terms of their chemical or active sites. Metal−organic framework (MOF)-integrated electrospun membranes and their relationships between the framework chemistry, membrane architecture, removal mechanisms, stability, and fabrication were critically examined. We can identify membranes as selective barriers from those as adsorbent/catalyst scaffolds, batch and continuous flow performance data, and experimental evidence for proposed removal mechanisms. MOF-based membranes have high potential for the removal of heavy metals and antibiotics, or to gain photocatalytic properties, but are challenged by active site blocking, aggregation, aqueous stability, and scale-up. Although limited by their synthesis complexity, cost, crystallinity, organic pollutant removal, and mechanical stability, covalent organic framework (COF)-based membranes have complementary benefits in terms of chemical stability, tunable porosity, antifouling, and oil−water separation. While their complementary properties facilitate MOF−COF hybridization, the performance of the membranes greatly relies on the interfacial chemistry, the ratio of the components, the dispersion, and the formation of defects. Electrospun MOF−COF membranes for wastewater treatment remain largely unexplored and are discussed here as an outlook. Controlled interfacial design, water-stable framework combinations, realistic wastewater validation, and scalable fabrication strategies are therefore needed for future progress.

institutions: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay

works.abstract: Abstract The persistent presence of emerging contaminants, including antibiotics and endocrine-disrupting compounds, in aquatic environments poses significant environmental and public health challenges. Standalone biological and electrochemical advanced oxidation processes each face significant limitations in effectively removing emerging contaminants. Therefore, integrating these technologies offers a promising approach to bridging performance gaps and enhancing overall contaminant removal in wastewater treatment. This study develops an integrated electroconductive membrane bioreactor (EMBR) that combines a bioreactor with a side-stream electroconductive membrane, enabling efficient removal of emerging contaminants and effective control of fouling. It details the fabrication and application of laser-induced graphene (LIG)-incorporated polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) composite electroconductive membranes (LIGPVDF ECMs) prepared via the nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) method. The membranes were integrated into the EMBR and assessed for their ability to remove and degrade amoxicillin (AMX), bisphenol A (BPA), and ciprofloxacin (CIP). Despite their ultrafiltration pore sizes, the LIGPVDF membranes achieved up to ∼99% removal at low applied voltages (1–3 V), comparable to nanofiltration membranes. The performance was also evaluated across different pH conditions in crossflow filtration mode using synthetic wastewater. High removal was attributed to electrochemical oxidation, electro-adsorption, and Donnan exclusion. In addition to pollutant removal, cathodic LIGPVDF potentials reduced fouling to 13% flux decline (vs &gt;50% anodic), while electrocleaning restored ∼91% flux from bioreactor effluent, outperforming DI cleaning (∼68%). The findings provide a pathway for developing hybrid, energy-efficient treatment technologies that target emerging contaminants under environmentally relevant conditions.

works.abstract: Abstract Nonfluorinated proton exchange membranes for all-vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) typically exhibit a trade-off between proton conductivity and vanadium ion barrier performance. Here, a design strategy is proposed for the preparation of composite membranes by casting sulfonated polyether ether ketone (SPEEK)/sulfonated polyaryl ether sulfone (SPAES) onto ZIF-8-modified polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) substrates. The effects of ZIF-8 growth time, which was used to vary the ZIF-8 loading, on the structural stability, electrochemical properties, and single-cell performance of the composite membranes were systematically investigated. The results show that the membrane with an in situ growth time of 12 h for ZIF-8 (denoted as SK-12@PTFE) exhibits optimal overall performance. Its ion selectivity reaches as high as 2943.17 × 104 S·min·cm–3, which is significantly superior to that of Nafion 212. In single-cell tests at 80 mA·cm–2, the SK-12@PTFE membrane delivers a Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 98.9%, an energy efficiency (EE) stabilizing at 72%–74%, and a peak power density of 248 mW·cm–2 at 250 mA·cm–2. The self-discharge time was extended to 480 h, and the membrane remained structurally intact after 20 days of immersion in a strongly oxidizing electrolyte. The −N–H groups of imidazole in ZIF-8 form an acid–base hydrogen-bonding network with sulfonic acid groups, providing a hopping pathway for protons, thereby enhancing proton conductivity. This strategy offers a viable technical route for developing high-performance nonfluorinated composite membranes for VRFB applications.

works.title: A Proposed Phenomenological Material–Energy Scaling Framework for Recovery-Constrained Solvent Sustainability
works.abstract: Solvents constitute a major material and environmental burden in pharmaceutical manufacturing, yet sustainability assessment is still largely based on proportional metrics such as Process Mass Intensity (PMI) and aggregated life-cycle indicators. Building on our previously published solvent-centric sustainability framework, which integrated PMI, circular PMI (cPMI), Global Warming Potential (GWP), and Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) for solvent-focused process assessment, the present study develops a phenomenological material–energy scaling formulation for recovery-constrained solvent sustainability. The proposed relationship is formulated as a testable phenomenological scaling framework, with its present scope limited to a system-specific relationship rather than a universal physical law. The framework represents the total sustainability burden, L(η), as a combination of a material-driven contribution and a recovery-associated nonlinear contribution: L(η) = c + kM(η) + β[ηn/(1 − η)], where M(η) is solvent material intensity, η is the recovery fraction, c is an intercept, k is a material-impact coefficient, β represents system-specific recovery-associated sensitivity, and n is a phenomenological recovery exponent. A dimensionless form is: L* = c* + αM* + λ[ηn/(1 − η)], where L* = L/L0, M* = M/M0, c* = c/L0, α = kM0/L0, and λ = β/L0. The nonlinear coordinate, Φ(η;n) = ηn/(1 − η), is used as a practical representation of recovery-associated asymptotic behaviour rather than as a first-principles thermodynamic equation. The parameters β, λ, and n are therefore expected to depend on the solvent, process configuration, recovery technology, operating conditions, response being measured, and system boundary. A seven-record pharmaceutical case-study dataset was used to examine the linear material relationship, the proposed nonlinear recovery coordinate, and an extended material–recovery interaction. Across the records, solvent mass decreases from 150 to 45 kg·kg−1 API as recovery increases from 30% to 92%, while energy use decreases from 520 to 380 MJ·kg−1 API. The linear model explains most of the observed variation (R2 = 0.979), whereas adding the nonlinear recovery term provides only a small improvement (R2 = 0.981), is penalized by information criteria, and gives an exponent at its imposed upper limit. An extended interaction model gives a closer fit to the seven observations, but its five-parameter structure relative to only seven observations does not support claims of independent predictive performance. These results therefore provide a basis for treating the proposed formulation as a testable phenomenological scaling hypothesis, rather than as evidence for a universal material–energy law. A complementary step-resolved analysis examines how solvent-related material and environmental burdens are distributed across individual process operations and how recovery may shift the balance between material use and recovery-associated energy requirements. This analysis identifies high-contributing operations and defines an Impact Concentration (IC) Index: IC = Σi fi2, where fi = Li/Ltotal represents the fractional contribution of operation i to a specified sustainability burden. IC is used as a descriptive measure of burden concentration and process localization, rather than as a thermodynamic variable, causal parameter, or universal recovery criterion. Thus, the step-resolved analysis identifies where burdens are concentrated, while the scaling formulation examines how material intensity and recovery-associated burden may be related. Solvent-level descriptor and impact analyses show substantial variation in GWP and CED among the supplied solvents, while exploratory machine-learning analysis indicates the potential for relating molecular descriptors to solvent sustainability. These analyses remain exploratory because of their small sample sizes and differences in data sources and system boundaries. A separate desalination comparison examines whether similar recovery–energy patterns can be observed across other recovery-constrained separation systems. Because membrane, thermal, and solvent-recovery processes differ in their mechanisms, feed characteristics, product requirements, and energy use, this comparison is treated as an empirical comparison of recovery–energy relationships rather than evidence of a common physical mechanism or universal master curve. Finally, a compact cross-domain analysis using 24 observations from independent recovery-related datasets examines whether the proposed recovery coordinate can also provide a useful comparative description beyond pharmaceutical solvent systems. The exponent was not refitted to create a new universal relationship. Furthermore, the broader, forward-looking exergy-based Computational Sustainability Physics (CSP) framework, representing an original conceptual development by the present author, has not included in this study. Overall, the results indicate a system-specific and testable material–energy scaling framework in which increasing solvent recovery can reduce virgin-material demand while changing the relative importance of recovery-associated energy and process-level burden concentration. Further studies using independently documented process data, wider recovery ranges, consistent system boundaries, and independent validation across different solvents and recovery technologies are needed to determine the broader predictive value and transferability of the proposed formulation.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) could enable safer, high‐energy‐density lithium‐metal batteries (LMBs), but practical use is limited by the trade‐off between fast Li‐ion transport and mechanical strength needed to suppress dendrites. Herein, we report an additive manufacturing approach based on photopolymerization‐induced microphase separation (photo‐PIMS) for the fabrication of customized, nanostructured SPEs with spatially and chemically segregated soft ion‐conducting and hard mechanically reinforcing domains in a single step. Chain extension of poly[oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl ether acrylate] (POEGMEA) macromolecular chain transfer agents (macroCTAs) with isobornyl acrylate and trimethylolpropane triacrylate drives microphase separation to form a bicontinuous nanostructure. The resulting membranes show a room‐temperature Li‐ion conductivity of ∼1 mS cm −1 with a shear modulus of 110 MPa. The optimized SPE membrane shows oxidative stability up to ∼4.5 V against Li/Li + and sustains stable Li plating/stripping for 1000 h at 0.5 mAh cm −2 . As an initial demonstration of device compatibility, a Li metal full cell with LiNi 1/3 Mn 1/3 Co 1/3 O 2 delivered specific capacities of 120 and 85 mAh g −1 at 0.5C and 1C, respectively, retaining 94% of the initial capacity after 20 cycles at 0.5C and ∼80% after 100 cycles at 1C. This work establishes photo‐PIMS as an efficient route to customized, nanostructured SPEs for LMBs.

works.abstract: Abstract Addressing the issue of low ionic conductivity in poly(vinyl butyral) (PVB)/poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)‐based solid‐state polymer electrolytes, a γ ‐butyrolactone (GBL)‐modified PVB/PMMA–lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) solid‐state polymer electrolyte membrane was prepared using propylene carbonate (PC) as the solvent and introducing GBL as a co‐solvent for plasticization, employing the hot‐pressing method. The effects of PC/GBL ratio on the microstructure, ionic conductivity, mechanical properties, optical properties, and thermal stability of the electrolyte membrane were systematically investigated. Furthermore, WO₃‐based electrochromic devices were assembled to evaluate device performance. The results showed that the addition of an appropriate amount of GBL could reduce the system viscosity, promote lithium salt dissociation and lithium‐ion migration, and improve the mobility of polymer segments, thereby constructing continuous ion transport channels. When the mass ratio of PC to GBL was 2:1 (BAPG‐4), the electrolyte exhibited optimal comprehensive performance, with an ionic conductivity of 3.26 × 10 −5 S cm −1 at room temperature and a low ionic migration activation energy of 0.18 eV. This electrolyte membrane also demonstrated good visible light transmittance, mechanical strength, fracture ductility, interfacial adhesion, and thermal stability, meeting the operational requirements of the device. The electrochromic device assembled based on the BAPG‐4 membrane exhibited excellent redox reversibility and ionic diffusion kinetics, achieving an optical modulation amplitude of 63.8% at a driving voltage of −3 V. After 2000 electrochemical cycles, the device exhibited slight performance degradation, which can be further improved by optimizing the GBL ratio to enhance long‐term cyclic stability. This PC/GBL compound plasticization strategy provides a reference for the development of high‐performance transparent solid‐state electrolyte membranes and sandwich‐type safe electrochromic devices. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

works.title: Solar assisted lithium recovery from brines: challenges and opportunities for integrated system
institutions: University of California, Berkeley
works.abstract: The rapid projected increases in demand for batteries over the upcoming decades requires a large expansion of lithium production capacity. While hard rock mining currently dominates the worldwide production, brines hold over 60% of global lithium reserves. Lithium production from brines is hampered by low lithium concentrations and high concentrations of other interfering ions such as magnesium. This review comprehensively analyzes integrated solar evaporation methods for capturing the lithium in brines. By firstly reviewing the conventional solar evaporation-chemical precipitation method, a currently commercialized technique, we identify several key challenges, including long timescales, large environmental impacts, and issues capturing lithium in some brine chemistries which prevents it from being applied in more places. A promising strategy to address these challenges is integrating interfacial solar evaporation with adsorption materials. This integration presents several advantages, such as producing both high evaporation and lithium adsorption rates and separating lithium from interfering ions. However, a key issue that needs careful evaluation is scaling taking place on the evaporative surface over time, which can cause significant drops in evaporative flux, thereby lowering the effectiveness of this integrated method. Several anti-scaling technologies have been reported, among which integrated membrane and solar evaporation systems demonstrate excellent potential in maintaining long-term performance of high evaporation and lithium capture rates. Ultimately, integrating interfacial solar evaporation with adsorption/membrane processes has the potential to provide a versatile and sustainable method for capturing lithium from brines with complex compositions.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial solar evaporation represents a sustainable path to freshwater generation, yet its practical implementation is often hampered by the intrinsic trade‐off between high evaporation rates and salt accumulation. Here, we report a bioinspired, three‐dimensional solar evaporator derived from the carbonized pith of corn stalks. Its innate architecture, featuring a hierarchical porous structure with vertically aligned channels, enables lateral thermal insulation and longitudinal water transport. This structure spontaneously establishes continuous water‐salt cycling through a coupled vertical‐lateral salt cycling mechanism, effectively preventing salt crystallization. The optimized evaporator achieves an evaporation rate of 1.89 kg m − 2 h − 1 under one‐sun illumination and maintains a high rate of 1.72 kg m − 2 h − 1 in 20 wt.% NaCl brine over 12 h without salt accumulation. It also demonstrates exceptional long‐term stability, retaining performance after 30 days of immersion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl and exhibiting versatile purification capabilities for organic pollutants and ions. This work provides a scalable, structural blueprint for high‐performance solar desalination and wastewater remediation.

works.abstract: Decarbonization is a global priority for achieving sustainable future in alignment with the UN’s sustainable development goals by reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The water sector contributes approximately 10% of global GHG emissions due to its reliance on fossil fuels and the energy-intensive technologies used in water desalination. This study investigates the potential of integrating green hydrogen technologies with renewable energy into desalination processes, focusing particularly on the compatibility between hydrogen-based energy supply and desalination energy demand. Using a hybrid methodology that combines decision-making techniques with expert insights, this study systematically analyzes and prioritizes the main factors influencing the viability and effectiveness of this integration while developing strategic pathways to decarbonize desalination processes. Additionally, a supply–demand matching assessment evaluates operational alignment between various hydrogen-to-electricity conversion technologies and desalination systems. The findings demonstrate that while 57.1% of experts strongly support hydrogen-powered desalination, technical barriers such as renewable energy intermittency, limited technological maturity, and high energy costs pose significant challenges. The study suggests strategies that highlight the importance of targeted research and development (R&D), infrastructure development, and supportive policy frameworks to enable the scalable deployment of green hydrogen in the water sector, especially in developing countries and water-scarce regions, where it can help address both clean energy and water challenges under sustainable development goal frameworks.

works.abstract: Nano sphere and nano rod morphologies of Ceria nanoparticles were synthesized by precipitation and hydrothermal methods. UV-visible spectra showed lower band gap of nanorod morphology which was found to be more effective Photocatalyst for MB dye degradation. This nanorod morphology of Ceria was selected for incorporation into PVDF matrix by simple phase inversion method. Inclusion of these Ceria nanorods in PVDF causes transformation of α phase to electroactive β-phase. Characterization techniques such as Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed the (38% to 85%) increase in β-phase with the gradual increase in (1-3 wt. %) of Ceria into PVDF membrane matrix. Different features unveiled to investigate the potential application of PVDF-Ceria membranes. Firstly, membrane permeation properties were studied and characterization of membrane surface composition analyzed by Scanning electron microscope (SEM), Atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). These examinations confirmed decreased in water contact angle from 100 º to 43 º, higher pure water flux 201 L/m²h to 660 L/m²h and higher mechanical strength. Secondly, Catalytic studies showed 99% MB dye degradation in just 20 minutes by ultrasonication assisted mechanical vibrations. Dye degradation mechanism and dye scavenger test revealed free radicals, mainly OH . is responsible for degradation within less time in the presence of mechanical vibrations. Finally, dielectric studies were also performed to confirm the β-phase formation in optimized PVDF-Ceria in comparison to pristine PVDF membrane. Higher dielectric constant and low tan loss factor accentuate its dielectric potential applications.

works.abstract: ABSTRACT Biomimetic nanochannel membranes enable enantioselective sensing but often face a trade‐off between selectivity and ion permeability. In this work, we report a cyclodextrin‐functionalized ionic nanochannel membrane based on sulfonated holey graphene oxide and sulfonated cellulose nanofibers (CD‐SHGO/SCNF) that integrates efficient ion flux with selective chiral recognition. In‐plane nanopores within graphene oxide establish interconnected transport pathways, while surface‐grafted cyclodextrins impart supramolecular chiral gating capability. Notably, the β‐cyclodextrin‐modified membrane achieves an enantioselectivity factor up to 37.8, representing a pronounced reversal and amplification of the weak D‐biased background response observed for the unmodified nanochannels, meanwhile with a linear L‐histidine detection range of 1 nM–50 µM and a detection limit of 0.404 nM. The system further demonstrates excellent reversibility and retains an L‐His‐dependent response in highly diluted fetal bovine serum, providing a preliminary proof‐of‐concept for chiral sensing in a biological matrix. Experimental and theoretical analyses attribute the response to stronger β‐cyclodextrin/L‐His host–guest interactions that modulate interfacial properties and ion transport. This work provides an effective strategy for constructing supramolecularly gated nanochannels with co‐optimized ionic transport and molecular recognition, and offers insights into chiral recognition mechanisms in confined nanofluidic systems.

works.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals the rules of component transformation and the mechanism of quality formation of Phyllanthi Fructus during natural sun-drying process
institutions: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
Sichuan Nursing Vocational College
works.abstract: Natural sun-drying facilitates quality formation of Phyllanthi Fructus (PF) via enhanced accumulation of bioactive constituents. Nevertheless, its underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood, which impedes standardized quality control for this medicinal herb. In this study, transcriptomic and metabolomic approaches were integrated to systematically investigate time-course alterations in gene expression and metabolite abundance throughout an 11-day natural sun-drying process. Microstructural observations demonstrated that PF fruit cells retained intact morphological structures during the first four drying days, suggesting potential stress-triggered physiological responses. Key bioactive compounds such as gallic acid, chebulagic acid, ellagic acid and punicalagin gradually accumulated and peaked on day 8 of sun-drying. Transcriptome analysis identified 2,515 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with 1,261 up-regulated and 1,254 down-regulated transcripts. Functional enrichment showed these DEGs were principally enriched in three secondary-metabolism-related pathways: Phenylpropanoid biosynthesis (53 DEGs), flavone and flavonol biosynthesis (8 DEGs), and terpenoid backbone biosynthesis (23 DEGs). Metabolomics further annotated 58 differential metabolites largely involved in unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, as well as flavonoid biosynthesis. These metabolic pathways are tightly linked to plant adaptive responses to combined dehydration-heat stress during post-harvest sun-drying. Abstract The present results demonstrate that drought and heat stress generated during natural sun-drying processing are capable of triggering secondary metabolism, promoting the enrichment of bioactive compounds and elevating the medicinal quality of PF, which lays a solid scientific foundation for the optimization of processing strategies and formulation of quality evaluation criteria.
